A well maintained walking track linking Choof Choof Campground with Furnell Landing, enjoy the walk or have a fish off the rocks
Some steep sections on gravel but well worth the walk to the tunnel.
Short walk through to the Reservoir Wall or continue on to Youngs Creek. Alternatively start at Youngs Creek Picnic Ground and take the return walk.

A walking track in typical lowland forest between the East Gippsland Rail Trail and the Princes Hwy. This track is part of a greater loop encompassing the Nowa Nowa Arm foreshore and Lake Tyers State Park.

This walk commences at Deptford Picnic Area and traverses the slopes above the Nicholson River. The track passes through the forest over usually dry creek beds and provides views down to the Nicholson River.
This short loop, built for all-abilities, follows a formed gravel path with rest stops and interpretive signs along the way.

This walk meanders along the scenic Avon River and provides rewarding views and access to the river in several sections including The Channels. Vegetation varies from riparian species and wildflowers to dry sclerophyll forest on the rocky outcrops above. This is the main walk in the Avon - Mt Hedric

Mt Hedrick Walking Track is a scenic walk which predominantly follows a ridgeline from Mt Hedrick to Huggetts Lookout. Stunning views are available to the North with unique rocky outcrops and boulders providing an insight into the geology of the Avon - Mt Hedrick Natural Features and Scenic Reserve.

From the Channel lookout, follow the stairs down to the Avon river. This 2.1km grade 3 walk follows the Avon river through the spectacular channel gorge. The track is part of the extended Avon walking track.

This walk is a 1.5km circuit with the option of ducking down to the rocks themselves around 500m metres along the trail from the carpark end of the walk. Spectacular views of the rocks can be found midwalk on the main trail although caution should be taken around the cliffs near this section. The fi

The walk is approximately 1.8km  one way and provides access onto the Avon Walking Track with stunning views of the Avon River and surrounding hills. An 8 km walk through open snow gum forest that circumnavigates the Dinner Plain village. The walk has a rough, rocky track surface with some short steep hills. The track is generally under snow in the winter months.
Gravelled paths wind around the arboretum, with views to the surrounding hills.

After leaving the Memorial, this walk takes you to the north above the Reform Mine entrance. Along this walk you will see the towns old water storage basin (1934) which has long since been replaced. This small reservoir held water that was gravity-fed into town. The climb follows the drier northerly
The steady climb to the top rewards you with views over Bright as well as Mt.Feathertop, Mt.Fainter, and Mt.Bogong, the highest peak in Victoria. Return the same way.

This short historic walk of about 100 metres is suitable for young families, although parents need to be mindful of the steep escarpment beyond the barriers. The area is recovering from being burnt in the Beechworth-Library Road bushfire of 2009.

After leaving the Memorial, a steep track will take you past the entrance to the Reform Mine and an old ventilation shaft, which once serviced the Reform Mine. The track continues in a southerly direction where more sheltered conditions enable tree species such as Red Box and Long-leaf Box to flouri

The return walk to the lookout begins at the J.A. Jones Memorial Reserve on the eastern edge of town adjacent to the Murray toMountains Rail Trail. The track makes a loop around a dam built in 1892 to provide a permanent supply of water to the town and railway station. It no longer provides water to Bright but makes for a pleasant short walk close to Bright.

The track makes a loop around the upper dam that was built in 1916 to provide a permanent supply of water to the town and railway station. It no longer provides water to Bright but offers a short walk close to Bright. Combine with lower loop for a longer walk.
Steepish but short walk up to the lookout over Bright.
A steady climb above Bright through quiet eucalypt forest. Return the same way.
This track connects the Mitta Mitta Historic Reserve and The Mill camp site.  It is a pleasant walk through streamside vegetation with constant views of the powerful Mitta Mitta river.

This track offers a base level walk starting from the Mitta Mitta Historic Reserve winding through forest and traversing Deep Gully with its temperate rainforest vegetation. Once out of the gully, the track leads through open forest of narrow leaf peppermint trees.

This walk takes you along the old water race previously used in the mining days, discover the old town water supply where water was delivered to the town using the old water race from the water race dam.

Take a slow walk along the meandering Goulburn river, peer into the shallow water and you may be able to spot a fish swimming past. Walk past the mini golf and try your luck at a hole in one, pass through some historic mining relics of yester year and finish up at the helipad which was once a tennis
A short steep walk that takes you up to expansive views across the valley, including the small township of Woods Point.

Get glimpses over Goughs Bay and the Delatite Arm through the newly regenerated surrounding forest. This site was once a pine plantation and has since been revegetated with forest species to the area. A steep track takes you up to the peak at the top, a walk often used by local residents of Goughs B

A beautiful walk through the wet montane forest, you will surround yourself with tall tree ferns and if you're quiet enough may hear or spot a lyrebird running about. The walk ends with a stunning view of the waterfall.

A gentle walk along the banks of the East Kiewa River. Stroll through riparian forest, with plenty of spots to watch the crystal-clear waters of the East Kiewa River. Along the track you will come across Mermaid Beach (250m) or Rockpool (800m), ideal spots for a picnic or a cool dip in the water. Th
This track links the Stringybark Camping Area with the start of the Stringybark Creek Historic Loop Walk.

Stop in at the Stringybark Creek Historic Reserve to get your dose of local history. This is the spot that the infamous Kelly gang shot and killed three police officers (Constables Lonigan, Scanlan and sergent Kennedy) in 1878. This track visits the key sites of this event, with on-site information

This is an easy walk through the Box-Ironbark forest to Dunns Reef. Elevator Walking track is a 5 km return which starts at the lower trailhead of the Mt Taylor mountain bike park. It is signposted from the lower trailhead and heads uphill on a narrow winding track. This walk loops either side of the Werribee River between the Werribee River Picnic Area and Carrolls Springs Picnic Area. The walk follows the Werribee River through beautiful mixed species eucalypt forest, alive with birdsong and the occasional thump of wallabies retreating from approaching walker

Stevensons Falls is one of the Otway regions most accessible and spectacular waterfalls. Starting from the car park, this short walk passes through a strand of giant Californian redwood trees, remnant of a trial plantation established in the 1980s. This walk follows a historic tramline where horses and later, steam locomotives once hauled logs out of the forest. Begin at the Powelltown picnic area across from the DELWP office. Follow the signs to cross the Little Yarra River and head up the stairs to access the old Reids Tramline route. Along

This walk starts from the picnic area and heads down through the forest and along the Latrobe River. The walk ends in an open grassy area by the river. Relax by the river and when ready, retrace your steps back to the Latrobe River Picnic and Camping Area.

This walk starts across the road from the Cascades Picnic Area. The walk drops down through the forested valley to the Murrindindi River, via a track and a series of steps and stairs. Two bridges span the river, giving you views of the river as it cascades down a rocky face. Enjoy the view and then

Situated in the centre of Marlo, this track network is a nice place to spend an hour strolling through the Marlo State Forest in a choose your own adventure series of short walks, linking up with the main streets in Marlo.

This is a short walk up a sandy rise to a viewing platform, with 360-degree panoramic views of the surrounding desert from the viewing platform. On a clear night, it's a great place to star-gaze away from all light pollution.
Walking track linking the Cassinia and Sec camping areas

This is a relaxing walk along a nice flat track through a beautiful patch of forest, with views along the boundary track into surrounding farmland. Walk off your breakfast or get your morning run ticked off..

Follow what was once an old road (Middle Tyers Road) and walk underneath ancient Mountain Ash and Myrtle Beech. Enjoy glimpses of giant granite bolders along the walk and the diversity of plants, from the unique assemblage of flora to the mosses and fungi that cover the forest.

Experience the area's rich gold mining history and immerse yourself in the rugged beauty of the Thomson River and surrounding mountainous valleys with this walk. The area’s dense forest is abundant with wildlife, and in early spring it becomes golden with flowering wattles.

This loop starts and finishes at Poverty Reef, which can be accessed via the Lookout loop. This walk takes in the northern section of Reform Hill, formally the site of the school pine plantation and has been replanted with native vegetation since 2011. The walk leads to an excellent lookout, overloo

Meringtons Walk follows the route to the gravesite of Charles Brown near the Meringtons Campground. The majority of the track is well maintained and clearly defined, but access to the grave requires wading through the Aberfeldy River. River depths vary per season so proceed with caution when crossin

Store Point was once a township established for the Donnellys Creek gold mining boom in the 1860s.

The Store Point Historic Loop Walk starts from the Store Point Hut, and follows McKean Creek upsteam.  The loop taks you to the Store Point Burial Ground, schoolhouse site and past various old house s
The Crinoline Walk starts past the Morning Star Mine the walk and continues on to the Crinoline battery built in the gold mining days to service the Morning Star Gold Mine

While exploring the old Red Jacket township site, make sure you visit the old cemetery site. The short walk climbs from the town centre into the cemetery. Explore the gravestones of the people that once lived in this mining ghost town.
Explore relics of the old Red Jacket ghost town. This track climbs up to the site of an old boiler and various other old relics left over from the towns mining past.

Commencing from the Jack Cann Reserve, the walk heads north east following the Lerderderg River, through mixed species eucalypt forest. After approximately 4 km, it loops around to head back towards Jack Cann Reserve. This return section is also part of the longer Great Dividing Trail.

This walking track runs along the river corridor from the Toorongo Falls campgrounds up to the Toorongo Falls Picnic Area. From there you can link up for a longer walk to the Toorongo Falls Walk, to view the falls

A short, steep pleasant walk rewards walkers with spectacular granite boulder formations and views over the Strathbogies. This track links the James Reserve campground to the Lima East Day Visitor Area and also provides access onto the Lima East Boulders Walk.

A pleasant walk around the perimeter of Annya Swamp through Lowland Forest. A flat formed track that should take between 1 to 1.5 hours to complete. There are several quiet spots to stop and enjoy the serenity or stop at the bird hide overlooking the swamp to quietly observe a rich diversity of bird

This walk passes through beautiful Mountain Ash forests and down into cool temperate rainforest, with highlights that include crossing an impressive timber trestle bridge, a look inside a small heritage-listed sawmill and walking along the aqueduct that feeds the Royston Power Station. The Rubicon V

This walk takes in most of the Rubicon Heritage Walk, passing through beautiful Mountain Ash forests and sections of cool temperate rainforest, crossing an impressive timber trestle bridge and walking along the aqueduct that feeds the Royston Power Station. It also then loops out to Rubicon Dam and

routes.name: Link trail to Rocky Ned Falls Walk

sourceTags.walkingComment: This link walking track provides access onto the Rocky Ned Falls walk and also down to Rocky Ned Creek

A hidden waterfall nestled in the heart of the Upper Murray, Thowgla Falls is located off Marginal Road in the Thowgla Valley, about 50km south of Corryong. The walk crosses three footbridges through native bushland and ferns on a well-formed track up to a viewing platform with views to the falls.

Whalers Lookout walking track is a short loop that travels through messmate forest, ending in a lookout with spectacular views across Portland Bay, overlooking farmland, the township of Narrawong and the Southern Ocean beyond. Along the way, you may be lucky enough to spot koalas, echidnas, wallabie

The Redwoods Boardwalk offers a short diversion off the main Stevensons Fall Walk for those returning from the falls viewing platform. It takes you through the dappled light of a stand of mature Californian Redwood trees, before returning back to the main track.

The Blue Spruce Walk is a short walk under a stand of Blue Spruce trees and runs alongside the Gellibrand River, providing views into the river and surrounds. There are seats along the walk to allow you to stop and soak in the views.
This short walk takes you up to a viewing platform with expansive views out over the State forest and across into the Murray Sunset National Park.

A short, well-formed trail that leads from the picnic area to the memorial site. The trail descends from the picnic area into the next gully along a well signed path. At 150m (one way) in length, the trail finishes at the memorial site surrounded by native forest. Some seating is provided for those

This short uphill walk takes you to a stand of Redwood trees that was part of an earlier planting trial into the suitability of Redwoods for timber production. See the Redwoods battle it out with the native eucalypts for survival.

routes.name: Link track between picnic area and campground

sourceTags.walkingComment: This track provides pedestrian access between the day visitor area and the camping area.

A beautiful loop walk through tall wet forest and taking in the picturesque riverine environment along the Toorongo and Little Toorongo Rivers.  The pathway meanders upwards with formed track interspersed with artisan crafted rock stairs.  On the way distant glimpses of the Toorongo Falls give you a

This walk is situated in the Wombat State Forest and traverses part of the Great Dividing Trail but then loops down around Whipstick Creek through some beautiful open eucalypt forest, to bring you back to your starting point at the Jack Cann Reserve. routes.name: Access track to Stevensons Falls and day visitor area

sourceTags.walkingComment: This access track takes you from the back of the Stevensons Falls Campground up to the day visitor area and to the start of the walking track to Steavensons Falls.

A downhill trek from the camping area, the 20 metre high Beauchamp Falls is a gem nestled in the Otway Forest Park. This rainforest track winds along the cool and tranquil waters of Deppeler Creek. There is a viewing platform at the end that provides views of the waterfall dropping into a deep pool

Following the Yackandandah Creek, this shared use trail meanders through open eucalypt foothill forest. The walk meanders through mixed species forest across an undulating landscape to the site of a former sawmill (Andersons Mill) which milled trees in the late 1800's from the surrounding forests, carting the timber on horse-drawn trams to Tretham. Towards the Andersons Mill end of the walk you will c

This walk passes through tall open forest, carpeted with bracken and crosses a number of gullies to conclude at a picnic area. This walk follows a former water race dug by hand by miners with the help of horse and drays in 1870. Rewarding two day walk through tall eucalypt forest to open sub alpine vegetation. Walk features large granite boulders, Raglan Falls, extensive views across the western plains to the Grampians and steep tree fern lined gullies and tall eucalypts. The walk starts at Richards and is easily accessible

The walk runs alongside the Cave Hill Creek Education Centre for the first 0.5km before joining the loop of the walk, passing through mixed species eucalypt forest carpeted with bracken, skirting Cave Hill Creek and Fiery Creek. Paradise walk is a full half-day walk through beautiful Messmate and Manna Gum forests, up ridge tops and down through fern lined gullies and creek crossings. It involves several short boardwalk crossings, some short steep hills and sections of steps. The walk starts from The Glut picnic area - head

Borella Walk is a moderately steep walk up the southern track on Ben Nevis, providing views over the surrounding plains and out to the Grampians. Panoramic views can be had at the summit of Ben Nevis.
This short flat walk through the surrounding forest takes you directly to the Bilstons Tree, a large and imposing redgum.

One of the most challenging but beautiful walks in the area, the Wilhelmina track begins at Water Gauge Camp and heads over the suspension bridge along the Murrindindi River Walk, before turning right at the junction.  Here the track climbs gradually over rocky steps to the base of the Wilhelmina Fa

A short meandering path through the native forest will see the visitor immersed in a natural surrounding and enjoying the local bird life. The walk contains a longer, scenic loop, which takes the visitor on a longer path to discover what this site has to offer.

The Great Dividing Trail consists of four linked tracks stretching from Bacchus Marsh (40 km West of Melbourne) to the goldfield cities of Ballarat and Bendigo. Hermans Hill Track passes by Hermans Hill Lookout. The site was developed by the local community and Nhill Seconday School students and provides a great view of Lake Hindmarsh, farmland and the Big Desert.
Starting on the boundary of pine plantation and the state forest. Along this track you will see beautiful native flora and fauna, spectacular views and naturally occuring waterfalls.

One of the ultimate short walks in the Victorian High Country. At the beginning of the walk you are surrounded by tall Eucalypt forest then climb to Snow Gum woodland. The Howqua River Walking Track is a popular walk, this walk will take you a total of 12.4 km through stunning native vegetation. A pleasant after lunch walk, this track is signposted from the Waterfalls Picnic Area and follows the course of the No.2 Creek upstream to a rock outcropping. Water flows in the winter months only, or after heavy rainfall.
A steep four-wheel drive track leads to the start of this walk.  Numerous relics including chimneys, hut sites and diggings from an early mining settlement reward the walker.

The Pyrenees Endurance Walk is 18 km one way and is recommended as an overnight trip starting at the Waterfalls Picnic area with Cameron’s Track being the halfway point. This walk is considered to be reasonably difficult with some steep sections. In drier months, you will need to carry your own wate
This short walk takes you through historical mining relicts at the site, while taking in the beauty of the bush.

Follow the walking track from Battery Dam to the Bull Gully Rock Wells made by the Jaara Jaara people. The Ada Tree Walk meanders its way through cool temperate rainforest with groves of Sassafras, ancient Myrtle Beech and tree ferns towards a viewing platform at the Ada Tree, a giant Mountain Ash considered to be one of Victoria's largest trees.

This short walk leads to Seven Acre Rock, a granite rock outcrop which on a clear day provides commanding views of the Bunyip State Park, Western Port Bay and Port Phillip Bay. The walk starts from the Seven Acre Rock picnic area, 500 metres east of the junction of Learmonth Creek Road and Bunyip Ro

Descend down the Wilhelmina track and take in the stunning valley views before carefully stepping between

The walk starts in the Big Pats Recreation and Camp

Although predominately ridden by bike, this trail with its gentle grades, beautiful forests and interesting history is also a great walk. The times and distance for this trail assume starting point is where the Gippsland Lakes Discovery Trail joins the East Gippsland Rail Trail. If starting the walk

A 3 km stunning walk amongst the low snow gums with views across the surrounding alpine valleys, leading up to the historical Craigs hut. It is a well formed track with some short steep sections. A good way to visit Craigs Hut if you want to stretch your legs or for those in 2WD vehicles.
This walk meanders through Alpine Ash Forest and Riparian Thicket.
This walk crosses a branch of Bentley Creek and passes through tall Mountain Gum Forest
Kendalls Link Trail is a short 1.1 km walk that connects Kendalls Camp to the Boys Camp. This flat, well formed track is a great short stroll through the riparian bush.

Starting at The Boys Camp, this 6.1 km return loop takes in both sides of the Rubicon River. The trail meanders along the river for a large part of the walk which is perfect for taking in the sounds of the river, the birds and the rustling trees. Boroondara Track can be accessed from Falls Creek road carpark 700m from the Murrindindi road junction. This circuit track encompasses both Wilhelmina Falls and a section of Murrindindi Walk. There are a couple of benches along the trail and several interpretative signs if you'd like to know more about the flora and fauna native to this area

The Kalatha Giant Tree Walk is a short easy return trail that takes in the magnificent Kalatha Giant.  Thought to be over 350 years old, the large Mountain Ash tree is 73m tall with a girth of 16m. Situated at the foothills of the Rubicon State Forest, Snobs Banyarmbite Falls offers spectacular views as the pristine water fed by the Snobs Creek flows over the 100m drop of rocky outcrops. Located in the heart of the Big River State Forest, this gentle walk follows the banks of Big River through forests of Peppermint and opens to a picturesque cascading waterfall.

Flowing from the Monda road green break down the mountain this track winds under some large Mountain Ash and 1939 regeneration forest into fern gullies over numerous timber bridges.  Eventually you can head into the Wirrawilla Rainforest Walk and up the old Quarry road track back to Monda carpark.

You can begin the Myrtle Gully walk at either Tanglefoot picnic area or via Wirrawilla Rainforest.  This 9km track follows the Myrtle Creek under some amazing Myrtle Beech trees before rising into the Mountain Ash stands then dipping in to the gullies at the Tanglefoot boardwalk. Located in the centre of Toolangi township the Yea River Walk is a lovely short, relatively flat trail that meanders through beautiful mixed species forest and then under majestic Mountain Ash canopies. Take a short walk to Bindaree Falls, located in a tranquil setting you will be surrounded by lush native forest and magnificent tree ferns. The walking track begins at the back of the picnic area and gently winds its way downstream to the top of the Young's Creek waterfall. Here the creek surges over a rock face to plunge into a large pool some 13 metres below.
Nice moderate walk through remnant warm temperate rainforest.
Stretch your legs by taking a gentle walk through warm temperate rainforest, the walk is a loop so there is no need to retrace your steps.
A well formed path through gently undulating country forming the start of the greater wilderness walk through to Shipwreck Creek

This early 1900s railway line was built to carry timber from mills in the surrounding forest. Of the seven original bridges, only the Noojee trestle bridge remains. The Upper Yarra Walking Track is the oldest long distance walking track in Australia and it provides a challenging walk along old logging tramlines and old vehicle tracks finishing at Mt Whitelaw on the Alpine Walking Track. This walk meanders towards the Aberfeldy river from Donnelly’s Creek Rd, take in views of recovering forest and historic artefacts in the area. At the boiler you can return via the same route or take a slightly steeper return loop by crossing the bridge and following the trail up the southern slope.

This track through the Boola Boola State Forest and Tyers Park is a challenging walk with stunning bushland scenery. It is normally walked from Moondarra Dam off W18 track down to Wirilda Park in the Latrobe Valley, however some interescting roads enable the walk to be completed in shorter sections.
This walk loops off Easy Magic Walk and follows the service track behind residential properties then turns left before Engineers Road through the forest to return to the Easy Magic Walk.

A 3km walk through local forest that passes through undulating forest and crosses gullies and forest roads. The walk passes passes by an old concrete magazine which was once used for storing explosives for road building.

Wirrawilla Walk consists of timber boardwalk winding through cool temperate rainforest.  The ancient Myrtle Beech trees and Southern Sassafras provide a dense canopy that shades the understorey all year round. A 3km loop walk through local forest showcasing the forest types present on the drier ridges.

A 6km challenging circuit through local forest, with some steep sections including a steep descent into a gully before climbing onto the ridge. The track passes the old plane crash site and the Explosive Magazine site.

This 11km walk is great for the experienced bushwalker, following the Howqua Valley between Running Creek and Howqua Hills Track. Take in the breathtaking scenery of the surrounding hills and the river below you. There are some short steep hills and small obstacles along the path.

This walk takes you to the historic Morning Star waterwheel and mining relics of the Crinoline township. The walking track start off Middle Star Track. From the car-park this walk leads to both ends of the diversion tunnel, it has some occasional steep sections but is well worth the effort to take in the history of the area.

This is a short day walk which explores the historic Black Snake Creek mining area Southwest of Dargo. A small gully provides just enough moisture to provide a much different range of plant species to that of the surrounding dry ridge.

The walking track, as well as being interesting historically, traverses some very scenic forest with camp and picnic sites along the way. This walk takes you back to the Lees Creek alluvial gold mining era of the 1890s where you will be able to view old house sites, alluvial diggings and a water race used to bring water from a dam to the diggings. The Waanyarra Walking Track is a loop that starts and finishes at the Waanyarra Recreation Area. The walk takes you through old gold workings, what was once the old historic Waanyarra Township and past the old cemetery.

A pleasant walk through the Walmer State Forest taking in the beauty of box-ironbark forest.  A feature on the walk is Pipeline Track, the location of an old wooden pipeline which supplied Maldon with water from Harcourt.

routes.name: Koondrook Red Gum Forest Walk - Eagle Loop

sourceTags.walkingComment: For those who enjoy a leisurely walk, the Koondrook Red Gum Forest Walk - Eagle Loop is ideal. The walks passes through Red Gum forests and wetlands and links a number of historical, cultural and ecological sites of interest

routes.name: Koondrook Red Gum Forest Walk - Turtle Loop

sourceTags.walkingComment: If you're after a slightly longer half-day walk, then the Turtle Loop is ideal. The North Red Gums Walk is a largely flat open walk which provides a good idea of the vegetation which once covered the landscape in this district. Larger specimens of E. tereticornis can be found at the Northern end of the walk near the Recreation Reserve.
The South block displays similar vegetation to the North block with some slightly more open areas. It is reasonably flat and can easily be added onto the North loop if you wish to extend your walk.
The Middle Red Gums Walk cuts through the centre of the North block. This gets you further away from the access roads and provides a good example of the plains grassy woodland environment.

Red Hill Trail stretches up the side of Red Hill to one of the town's green breaks where there is an excellent view of Sugarloaf. The track then descending down to meet the Michaeldene Trail in the nearby gully. Turn right to return to Marysville.

A short link walk through private property joining the Michaeldene trail and the Tree Fern Gully Trail.  The trailhead can be found at the back of the Marysville recreation ground and over one of the steel bridges straddling the Steavenson River.
